method_rules.horizon_end: balance_date + horizon_months (month arithmetic, end of month clamped)
method_rules.run_rate_net_cash_flow_annual: operating cash flow + net cash used in investing + net cash used in financing - net debt issuance (every non-debt flow of the twelve months; new borrowing is excluded because committed undrawn funding is zero)
method_rules.maturities_in_horizon: principal of a facility whose maturity_date <= horizon_end, else 0
method_rules.amortisation_in_horizon: for a facility maturing after the horizon: min(annual_amortisation x horizon_months / 12, principal); 0 when it matures inside
method_rules.cash_at_horizon_end_before_refinancing: closing cash + run-rate over horizon - amortisation - maturities
method_rules.available_liquidity: closing cash + undrawn committed revolver (revolver commitment - revolver drawn); equals the CP-1 T4.10 liquidity fact, asserted
method_rules.resources_at_horizon_end: cash at horizon end before refinancing + undrawn committed revolver
method_rules.funding_gap: max(0, minimum cash - resources); a computed 0 is 'no gap', distinct from missing
method_rules.months_to_minimum_cash: run-rate cash flow alone (maturities and amortisation excluded; own limitation, the wall is in T2E.4/T2E.5). start = closing cash + undrawn revolver - minimum cash. Minimum cash missing: state 'missing' ('Not calculable: minimum cash not assessed'). Annual run-rate < 0: max(0, start) / (-annual / 12), 1 dp half-up. Annual >= 0: state 'not_reached' (text 'Not reached at run rate') when start >= 0, 0 months when start < 0. Revolver missing: 'not_reached' only when annual >= 0 and closing cash alone >= minimum cash (a revolver is never negative), else 'missing' ('Not calculable: revolver undisclosed'). The stored value is quantised to 1 dp ('20.0', never '2E+1')

own_limitations: Driver values are analyst assumptions without a source citation; no management guidance or consensus is an input.
The forecast is annual over three years from the CP-1 twelve-month base; no quarterly path is modelled.
Cash interest is the analyst's rate applied to the opening debt balance; no hedging, floor or reference-rate curve is modelled.
Cash taxes and working capital are modelled together as a share of revenue; no tax shield or working-capital cycle is modelled.

No new borrowing, refinancing or covenant waiver is modelled: debt moves only by the analyst's repayments, and cash is not floored, so a negative cash balance is an unfunded requirement, not a forecast of events.
The downside applies CP-2A's settled scenario shocks to every forecast year and holds revenue, capital expenditure, distributions and repayments at the base case; no mitigating action is modelled.
The break tests reuse CP-2A's levels, which are watch levels and definitions, not covenant tests; covenant compliance belongs to CP-4.
Accessible liquidity is closing cash plus CP-1's undrawn revolver; restricted, trapped or operationally required cash is not separated.
Debt maturities and refinancing feasibility are not modelled; the maturity wall and funding gap belong to CP-2D and CP-3C.
CP-1D (earnings quality) is not part of this run, so starting leverage is not restated on evidence-supported EBITDA and no comparison with it is made.
Minimum liquidity was not assessed, so the liquidity break test and liquidity headroom are not calculated.
In the downside case closing cash is negative from FY2028: an unfunded requirement, not a forecast of events.
A break test whose metric is not calculable in a forecast year is missing, with the reason, when no earlier year has met it.
Gap (Material): Earnings quality and minimum liquidity are not inputs to the forecast.

Forward headroom is only as reliable as the CP-2G forecast, which uses analyst-assumed drivers.
The migration view is the analyst's judgment on the published terms and the CP-2G path; no probability is computed, no rating is assigned and no agency action is predicted.
The notch difference is measured on the source's combined scale; outlook weighting and sub-notch differences are not modelled.
CP-1D (earnings quality) is not part of this run, so no earnings-quality adjustment is applied to the reported ratios.

Value available to claims is the enterprise value only: balance-sheet cash is not added and restructuring, administrative and financing costs are not deducted unless a claim class states them.

The waterfall applies strict priority by the analyst's rank number; classes of one rank share pro rata. Collateral value, guarantees, structural subordination and intercreditor terms are not modelled.

Enterprise value is the analyst's multiple applied to a CP-2G forecast EBITDA that rests on analyst-assumed drivers; it is not a market or court valuation.
The fulcrum is the first rank whose recovery is below its claim; the analyst's named fulcrum is checked against it. Plan treatment is checked for fit with the recovery, not for legal feasibility.
Recoveries are not probability-weighted and the valuations are not scenarios of equal likelihood.
